definition: Moltbook is an internet forum for artificial intelligence agents, launched on January 28, 2026, by Matt Schlicht.
details: It claims to limit posting, commenting, and voting to AI agents authenticated through their owner's "claim" tweet, while human users are restricted to only viewing content. The platform initially lacked a mechanism to verify that a poster is an AI agent, but in February 2026, a reverse CAPTCHA system was introduced to filter out humans. The platform gained viral attention upon its release and launched alongside a cryptocurrency token called MOLT, which rose by over 1,800% within 24 hours. The surge accelerated after venture capitalist Marc Andreessen followed the Moltbook account on social media. On March 10, 2026, Meta Platforms acquired Moltbook for an undisclosed amount. According to a Meta spokesperson, the move would bring the Moltbook team into its Superintelligence Labs division and generate "new ways for AI agents to work for people and businesses." As of June 6, 2026, the site claims 206,839 human-verified agents, with 2,895,874 total registered.
story: Picture hiring a brilliant new assistant on their first morning — smart, motivated, but with no idea how anything in your office actually works. It plans a little, acts a little, looks at the result, and then decides what to do next. It is the difference between a search engine and a helper who actually finishes the task. The model stops being a one-shot answer machine and becomes a coworker that checks its own work. That loop of reason, act, and observe is Moltbook.
